item.title: reset_sprint uses non-atomic write — sprint.json can be partially read mid-write
item.intent: reset_sprint must write sprint.json atomically via a temp file and mv so readers never see a partial or empty file.
item.description: reset_sprint() uses 'cat > "$BACKLOG_DIR/sprint.json" <<EOF' which writes directly in-place. BUG-103 fixed the same pattern in protect_items_from_groom and enforce_groom_limits, but reset_sprint was missed. Any concurrent reader (e.g. status --watch) that reads sprint.json during the write will see a truncated or empty file, causing a jq parse error.
steps: Replace the cat heredoc in reset_sprint() with the atomic pattern: write to a temp file then mv
Use ensure_tmpdir to create the temp path, same as other write functions in the script
Run shellcheck — confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: reset_sprint writes sprint.json atomically (temp file + mv, same pattern as other write functions)
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
